nodes.title: Semantic models (Power BI / Fabric): Key Ideas
nodes.content: A semantic model is the analytics layer that sits over your data — tables, relationships, measures, and hierarchies — that reports query. In Microsoft Fabric it's central to DP-600: how it stores and refreshes data drives performance.

flashcards.front: What lives in a semantic model?
flashcards.back: Tables and their relationships, calculated columns, measures written in DAX, hierarchies, and formatting/security (row-level security). Reports don't query the raw source directly — they query the semantic model, which is the single source of business logic.

flashcards.front: Import vs DirectQuery vs Direct Lake storage modes?
flashcards.back: Import copies data into the model (fastest queries, data is a snapshot until refresh). DirectQuery leaves data at source (always current, slower, pushes load to the source). Direct Lake reads Delta/Parquet in OneLake directly — near-Import speed with near-live freshness.

flashcards.front: What is a measure and why use DAX?
flashcards.back: A measure is a calculation evaluated at query time in the current filter context (e.g. Total Sales, YoY %). DAX is the expression language for measures and calculated columns; understanding filter and row context is the key to correct results.

RLS is defined in the semantic model with roles and DAX filter expressions that restrict which rows a user can see. It's enforced at the model layer, so every report and dashboard built on the model inherits the same access rules.

questions.q: An analytics engineer must build a Power BI semantic model in Microsoft Fabric that queries multi-billion-row Delta tables in a lakehouse with sub-second visual response times, without scheduling refreshes and without importing the data. Which storage mode delivers this?
choices: Import mode against the lakehouse SQL analytics endpoint with daily incremental refresh
DirectQuery against the lakehouse SQL analytics endpoint with auto-aggregations enabled
Direct Lake mode against the lakehouse Delta tables in OneLake
Composite mode combining DirectQuery to the warehouse and Import for lookup tables
questions.explanation: Direct Lake mode reads Parquet pages from the Delta tables in OneLake directly into the VertiPaq engine on demand, with no data duplication and no scheduled refresh. Import would require a copy and refresh schedule; DirectQuery pushes each query to the SQL endpoint which adds latency on large tables; composite mode still imports a slice. Direct Lake is the unique Fabric mode that combines Import-like speed with DirectQuery-like freshness.

questions.q: A team manages curated tables in an Azure SQL Database that must be queried from a Fabric lakehouse with near real-time freshness, no ETL code, and a single read-only Delta copy maintained automatically in OneLake. Which Fabric feature meets all three requirements?
choices: OneLake shortcut to the Azure SQL Database tables
Mirroring of the Azure SQL Database into Fabric
A Data Pipeline copy activity that runs every five minutes
A Dataflow Gen2 with incremental refresh into the lakehouse
questions.explanation: Fabric Mirroring continuously replicates an operational database (Azure SQL DB, Cosmos DB, Snowflake, etc.) into OneLake as read-only Delta tables with near real-time latency and no ETL to author. Shortcuts only work against file-based sources like ADLS Gen2 or another OneLake item, not against an Azure SQL DB. Pipelines and Dataflows are scheduled ETL with higher latency and code/maintenance overhead.

questions.q: An analytics engineer needs to enforce that sales managers only see rows for their assigned region in a Power BI report served from a Fabric semantic model. The same model is consumed by an Excel pivot and by a paginated report. Where should the row filter be implemented so it applies consistently across all clients?
choices: As a visual-level filter on every page of the Power BI report
As a WHERE clause in the SQL view that the semantic model imports from
As a row-level security (RLS) role with a DAX FILTER expression on the dimension table, mapped to the manager's UPN via USERPRINCIPALNAME()
As a Microsoft Purview sensitivity label on the workspace that limits row export
questions.explanation: Row-level security defined on the semantic model is enforced by the Analysis Services engine at query time, so it applies to every client that queries the model — Power BI, Excel via Analyze in Excel, paginated reports, and the XMLA endpoint. Visual filters can be bypassed by editing the report; SQL views only protect Import-time queries but not DirectQuery/Direct Lake refreshes initiated by other users; sensitivity labels classify and govern content but do not filter rows.

questions.q: A workspace administrator wants developers to author semantic models and reports in Visual Studio Code and Power BI Desktop, branch the work in Azure DevOps, and have changes promoted from Dev to Test to Prod with environment-specific connection strings. Which combination should be configured?
choices: Git integration on each workspace plus deployment pipelines with rules for connection-string parameters
Export each item as a .pbix file nightly and check it into the repo manually
A shared OneDrive folder for the .pbip projects and manual workspace-level overrides
Fabric REST APIs invoked from a single nightly Azure Function that overwrites Prod from Dev
questions.explanation: Fabric's Git integration syncs workspace items (semantic models, reports, notebooks, pipelines) as .pbip / source folders into an Azure DevOps or GitHub repo, giving developers branch-based authoring. Deployment pipelines then promote items Dev to Test to Prod with parameter and data-source rules to swap connection strings per environment. Manual .pbix exports, OneDrive sharing, or bespoke REST scripts lose lineage and lifecycle controls.

nodes.title: Direct Lake mode (Microsoft Fabric): Key Ideas
nodes.content: Direct Lake is a Fabric storage mode for semantic models that reads Delta/Parquet files in OneLake directly, with no import step and no per-query translation to the source. It targets DP-600's recurring theme: Import-like speed with DirectQuery-like freshness.

flashcards.front: How does Direct Lake differ from Import and DirectQuery?
flashcards.back: Import duplicates data and goes stale until refresh; DirectQuery is live but translates each query to the source. Direct Lake loads columns from OneLake Delta tables into memory on demand (paging) — no copy to maintain, and it reflects the latest committed Delta data.

flashcards.front: What backing storage does Direct Lake require?
flashcards.back: Delta/Parquet tables in OneLake — produced by a Fabric Lakehouse or Warehouse. Because it reads those files directly, the data must be in Delta format; non-Delta sources need to be loaded into a Lakehouse first.

If a query uses something Direct Lake can't serve from the Delta files (certain features or capacity limits), the engine can fall back to DirectQuery against the SQL endpoint. Minimising fallback keeps the speed advantage — a common tuning point.

flashcards.front: Why does Direct Lake matter for large models?
flashcards.back: It avoids the refresh window and memory cost of importing huge tables while still delivering interactive performance, because only the columns and rows a query touches are paged into memory from OneLake.

questions.q: A measure must return year-to-date Sales for the currently selected period in a report based on the date dimension marked as a date table. The model contains 'Sales'[Amount] and 'Date'[Date]. Which DAX expression is correct?
choices: Sales YTD = SUMX('Sales', 'Sales'[Amount])
Sales YTD = CALCULATE(SUM('Sales'[Amount]), DATESYTD('Date'[Date]))
Sales YTD = TOTALYTD(SUM('Sales'[Amount]))
Sales YTD = CALCULATE(SUM('Sales'[Amount]), ALL('Date'))
questions.explanation: CALCULATE with the DATESYTD time-intelligence function modifies the date filter context to all dates from January 1 up to and including the last date in the current filter context, producing year-to-date totals. TOTALYTD requires a date column as its second argument, so the syntax shown is incomplete and will error. SUMX without CALCULATE ignores time context, and CALCULATE with ALL('Date') removes all date filters, returning the grand total — not YTD.

questions.q: A Dataflow Gen2 cleans and joins multiple CSV files in ADLS Gen2, then publishes to a lakehouse table. Downstream queries that consume merged intermediate steps re-evaluate the source files on every refresh and the run is much slower than expected. Which change addresses the redundant work?
choices: Disable staging on all queries so they run end-to-end in the dataflow engine without intermediate writes
Enable staging on the intermediate merge queries so their outputs are materialized to the Fabric staging lakehouse and reused
Move the join logic into a downstream notebook and remove it from the dataflow
Convert the dataflow to a Data Pipeline copy activity with a tumbling window trigger
questions.explanation: When staging is enabled, Dataflow Gen2 materializes a query result to the hidden Fabric staging lakehouse / warehouse so downstream queries can read the staged data instead of re-evaluating the source. Disabling staging forces in-memory re-evaluation and makes the symptom worse. Moving logic to a notebook is a larger rewrite and not required. A Pipeline copy activity is a flat copy, not a Power Query transformation engine.

questions.q: An analytics engineer needs to query a Fabric semantic model from a Python notebook to validate measure results and pull table data into a pandas DataFrame for ad-hoc analysis, without exporting to CSV. Which Fabric capability should they use?
choices: The Power BI REST API GetQueryResults endpoint with manual JSON parsing
Semantic Link (the sempy library) inside a Fabric notebook
An on-premises data gateway with an ODBC driver pointing at the model
Copy the .pbix file to OneLake and read it with PyArrow
questions.explanation: Semantic Link (sempy) is the Fabric Python library that lets notebooks list workspace models, evaluate DAX measures, and materialize semantic-model tables as pandas DataFrames over the XMLA endpoint. The REST API does not return tabular query results in a DataFrame-friendly way, an on-prem gateway is for on-prem sources, and .pbix files are not designed to be parsed as Parquet by PyArrow.

questions.q: A semantic model in Direct Lake mode is consumed by a high-concurrency Power BI report. During peak hours users see queries fall back to DirectQuery, slowing visuals. Which two factors most commonly trigger this fallback? (Choose the option that lists both correctly.)
choices: Exceeding the SKU's column or row guardrails for Direct Lake, and the underlying Delta table being written to during the query
A measure using TIME-intelligence DAX functions, and the report using bookmarks
A composite model with an Import table, and the workspace being attached to a Pro license instead of a capacity
A user being assigned a row-level security role, and the model containing calculated columns
questions.explanation: Direct Lake falls back to DirectQuery on the lakehouse SQL endpoint when the model exceeds the capacity SKU guardrails (rows per table, columns per table, model size) or when the Delta table is being written to (framing in progress). Time-intelligence DAX, bookmarks, RLS, and calculated columns do not by themselves trigger fallback. A composite Import table is supported alongside Direct Lake without forcing fallback for the Direct Lake tables.

nodes.title: Microsoft Purview: Key Ideas
nodes.content: Microsoft Purview is the data governance, compliance, and protection suite for Microsoft 365 and beyond — classification, data loss prevention, retention, eDiscovery, and insider risk. It's the compliance counterpart to the security stack.

flashcards.back: Sensitivity labels classify and protect content (e.g. Confidential) and can enforce encryption, watermarks, and access restrictions that travel with the file. Labels can be applied manually or automatically based on content (e.g. detecting credit-card numbers).

flashcards.front: What does Data Loss Prevention (DLP) do?
flashcards.back: DLP detects sensitive information (PII, financial data) across email, Teams, SharePoint, OneDrive, and endpoints, and enforces actions — block, warn, or require justification — to stop it leaving the organisation. Policies are built from sensitive-info types.

flashcards.front: What is retention vs deletion in Purview?
flashcards.back: Retention policies and labels keep content for a required period (compliance) and/or delete it after a period (minimising risk). They resolve conflicts by a precedence order — retention generally wins over deletion to preserve records.

eDiscovery finds, holds, and exports content relevant to investigations or litigation across Microsoft 365. Legal holds preserve content in place so it can't be altered or deleted while a case is active.

questions.q: A team must analyze high-volume IoT telemetry arriving from Event Hubs with sub-second query latency over the last 30 days and KQL ad-hoc exploration, while keeping older data accessible for periodic reporting. Which Fabric item is the right primary store for the hot data?
choices: A lakehouse Delta table refreshed every minute by a Spark structured streaming job
A KQL Database in an Eventhouse, with OneLake availability turned on for the table
A Warehouse table populated by a Data Pipeline copy activity every minute
A Power BI Direct Lake semantic model with auto page refresh set to one second
questions.explanation: Eventhouse with a KQL Database is the Fabric Real-Time Intelligence engine designed for high-throughput time-series and log ingestion with sub-second KQL queries. Enabling OneLake availability also exposes the same data as Delta in OneLake so other engines can read it for reporting on older partitions. Minute-level Spark or Pipeline writes cannot match KQL latency, and a semantic model is a query layer, not a primary store.

questions.q: An analytics engineer needs to identify which DAX measure is causing a slow Power BI visual and inspect the storage-engine vs formula-engine time of each query. Which tool inside Power BI Desktop should they open first?
choices: Performance Analyzer, then copy the query into DAX Studio to view server timings
Query Diagnostics in Power Query Editor
View Native Query on the source
The Refresh History pane in the Power BI service
questions.explanation: Performance Analyzer in Power BI Desktop records each visual's DAX query and duration. The captured query can be copied into DAX Studio, where Server Timings break the duration into Storage Engine (SE) versus Formula Engine (FE) time and surface the actual queries sent to VertiPaq or DirectQuery. Query Diagnostics is for Power Query M, View Native Query inspects fold-down to the source, and Refresh History only shows dataset refresh runs.

questions.q: A semantic model defines 18 separate time-intelligence measures (MTD, QTD, YTD, PY, YoY%, etc.) for each of 12 base measures, resulting in over 200 measures and an unwieldy field list. Which feature consolidates the time-intelligence logic and presents users with a single 'Time Calculation' selector?
choices: Calculation groups in the semantic model
A composite model with an aggregations table
Field parameters in the report
Implicit measures on the date dimension
questions.explanation: Calculation groups define a set of calculation items (MTD, QTD, YTD, PY, YoY%) that can be applied to any explicit measure at query time, replacing N base measures times M variants with a single dimension users select. Field parameters swap which field is plotted but do not transform a measure. Composite models with aggregations are a performance pattern, and implicit measures (auto-aggregations on columns) cannot encode time-intelligence patterns.

questions.q: Governance requires that sensitive financial reports built in Fabric inherit the 'Confidential\Finance' classification from the source warehouse and that the label persists when users export to Excel or PowerPoint. Which capability enforces this end-to-end?
choices: Workspace-level access roles set to Contributor only
Microsoft Purview Information Protection sensitivity labels with inheritance configured on the semantic model and downstream items
A capacity-level workload setting that disables export to Excel
Row-level security roles that map finance UPNs to a hidden filter table
questions.explanation: Microsoft Purview Information Protection sensitivity labels can be applied to OneLake items, semantic models, and reports in Fabric. Inheritance propagates the source's label to downstream items and persists into exported Excel and PowerPoint files, where Azure Information Protection enforces the encryption and usage rights. Workspace roles control access, not classification; disabling export blocks a channel but does not classify content; RLS filters rows but does not label exports.
